definitions.corpus_line: {"id":"p0000".."p4999","text":...} UTF-8 LF, whitespace collapsed, no control chars
definitions.dense: last_hidden_state CLS row, L2-normalized (fp32); score = dot = cosine
definitions.gold_ids: passages the source dataset's human judgments mark relevant for that query (1..5 of them are in the corpus; nfcorpus queries with more judgments keep only their first 5 — see notes)
definitions.hybrid: not frozen: derivable as dense + alpha*sparse (bge-m3 default alpha 0.5)
definitions.matrix: float32 little-endian, row-major [query][passage], no header; row i is queries.jsonl line i (zero-padded id qNNN) and column j is corpus.jsonl line j (zero-padded id pNNNN)
definitions.query_src: provenance tag per query row: nfcorpus / miracl-zh-triples / mmarco-ja-triples / miracl-ko-triples for the 198 eval-set queries, synthetic-gibberish for the q198/q199 negative controls; corpus rows carry the same tags plus miracl-corpus-<lang> (cross-domain filler) and duplicate
definitions.ranking: sort by (-score, passage index ascending); groups of top-10 entries within |Δscore| < 1e-5 are reported unordered (plan §4.3)
definitions.sparse: lexical weight per token = relu(h @ W_sparse.T + b_sparse), W_sparse/b_sparse from sparse_linear.pt (fp16 values, fp32 math); kept for token ids > 2 (../golden_sparse.json convention), zero weights dropped, max-pooled per token id; score = sum of w_q*w_p over shared token ids, ascending token-id accumulation

gibberish_selection.rule: the GIBBERISH_N candidates with the lowest top dense score against the frozen corpus

gibberish_criterion.note: the reference model does not satisfy the literal §4.3 bound on real multilingual data: bge-m3 scores unrelated passage pairs below a noise string's best match, so the whole-matrix median is smaller than the gibberish max. Operationalise the control as (a) the engine's gibberish row must match these frozen golden values and (b) it must stay below the real-query top-1 score distribution recorded here.
gibberish_criterion.plan_4_3_literal: max dense score < median of the whole golden matrix
